title: Flux is its own image model again
summary:
Flux got its own lane, Gemini learned a few more tools, and Qwen Coder moved to Qwen3.

Requests for `flux` now use Flux Schnell instead of resolving to `zimage`, which remains the default. A separate SANA-Sprint 1.6B image-generation backend was also added, designed to generate images in two inference steps.

Gemini chat requests gained support for code execution, Google Search, and URL context. `gemini-search` defaults to Google Search, while callers can choose tools explicitly. Responses can now include generated plots and charts as `image_url` content blocks. A follow-up removed automatic code execution from `gemini-fast` so it works with structured-output requests.

The `qwen-coder` API name now routes to Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, with an 8,192-token maximum. Enter’s pricing page also shows human-readable model names and brings text, image, and video models into one sectioned table.

highlights.title: Flux gets its own lane
highlights.text: Choose `flux` for Flux Schnell instead of having the request resolve to `zimage`. `zimage` remains the default. [Browse Flux](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=flux).

highlights.title: More tools for Gemini
highlights.text: Use Gemini with code execution, Google Search, or URL context; pass a `tools` array to choose what a request uses. Generated charts can come back as `image_url` content blocks. [Explore the API](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).

highlights.title: Qwen Coder moves to Qwen3
highlights.text: `qwen-coder` now routes to Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, with an 8,192-token maximum. [Browse the model](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=qwen-coder).
